Further to the below emails, we are unable to proceed with the application for the following reasons:

  • The deed has not been dated on page 1.
  • The trustees and the adviser have signed the T001(TR) prior to 24/09/2026. The trustees and adviser need to correct this date to the same day or after the date of establishment of the trust. All amendments must be initialled.
  • The class of beneficiary “The Settlor’s children and further descendants” must be added to the TRS.

Dear Huw,
It was a pleasure to catch up at lunch last week. As promised, I attach a short executive summary of my proposals for your Rathbones investments, for you to consider at your leisure.
The headline numbers:

  • Your Transact portfolio grew by 17.00% over the last 12 months, a gain of about £1.22m after fees, and is up 54.78% over three years.
  • Over the same 12 months the Rathbones Strategic Growth and Enhanced Growth funds returned 5.28% and 6.37%, against between 9.5% and 17.4% for the Vanguard LifeStrategy range. Your Rathbones EIS portfolio is also about £167,000 (52%) below the amount invested.
  • Moving the Rathbones money (about £2.32m) to a lower-cost, evidence-based approach would reduce your annual charges from about £38,800 to about £21,200 under Option A (a saving of around £17,600 a year, circa £18,000). Option B would save at least as much if its fund and platform charges come in at or below those of Option A.
  • The VIP fee of about £8,400 a year falls away and is replaced by a single 0.05% charge across your whole portfolio, about £5,500. That is lower in pounds, and the paper shows how the new charge is shared between your Transact and Rathbones assets.
  • Selling would realise gains of about £403,700, but the tax losses within your EIS portfolio (about £103,600 after allowing for the income tax relief you have already received) reduce the net tax cost to between about £49,600 and £71,300, depending on how the losses are used. The cost is recovered through lower charges in around three to four years, and the tax is not payable until 31 January 2028.


Two options for reinvesting the money:

  • Option A: a new platform (Fundment) with Vanguard Life Strategy funds, at very low and transparent cost.
  • Option B: adding to your existing Transact portfolio and Dimensional funds, which keeps everything on one platform and statement and brings further economies of scale on a combined portfolio of about £11m. I am comfortable with either, or a split between the two.


Before any action I would need to confirm the purchase dates of your EIS holdings, as tax relief can be withdrawn on any shares sold within three years, and finalise the tax figures with the benefit of your income details and a Rathbones capital gains report. The figures are indicative at this stage, and past performance is not a guide to future returns.
Next steps:

  1. Please read the summary and let me know which option you prefer (A, B or a split), and whether you would like to proceed in whole or in stages.
  2. I will then confirm the Option B charges, the EIS dates and the tax position, and send you a full suitability report and fee confirmation before anything is done.
  3. I will also write separately to confirm the fee reduction following our move from the Vision network.
  4. Lasting Powers of Attorney remain important, and I will gently keep prompting you on that.


I will call you in a couple of weeks to hear your thoughts, but please do contact me sooner if you have any questions.
With best wishes for your trip to South Africa,
Jim
